1500855883.content:
Olá, equipe CapCut.

Gostaria de registrar uma crítica sobre a experiência com as ferramentas de geração de vídeo por IA.

Entendo perfeitamente a necessidade de proteger direitos de imagem, privacidade e identidade de pessoas reais. Essas são questões importantes e devem, sim, ser consideradas. O problema é quando o sistema passa a bloquear praticamente qualquer tentativa de criação, mesmo em situações legítimas de uso.

Na prática, a experiência está se tornando frustrante: você possui créditos para utilizar, possui imagens próprias e autorização para utilizá-las, mas não consegue gerar o conteúdo porque o sistema interpreta praticamente qualquer rosto como uma possível violação.

O resultado é contraditório: o usuário compra ou recebe créditos para utilizar uma ferramenta, mas não consegue efetivamente utilizar esses créditos nos projetos que precisa produzir.

Não estou defendendo que o CapCut libere indiscriminadamente a geração de vídeos com rostos reais. O que estou sugerindo é que exista uma solução mais inteligente.

Por exemplo:

* Uma opção de “Tenho autorização para utilizar esta imagem/pessoa”;
* Um sistema de confirmação de consentimento antes da geração;
* Diferenciação entre uso comercial autorizado e tentativa de impersonação;
* Possibilidade de utilizar imagens próprias como referência para movimentos simples de câmera, animações e transições;
* Maior transparência sobre por que determinada geração foi bloqueada;
* E, principalmente, alguma alternativa para que os créditos não sejam simplesmente inutilizados quando uma geração é recusada.

Hoje, muitas vezes, a sensação é:

“Você tem créditos, mas não pode usar.”

Isso prejudica justamente quem utiliza o CapCut profissionalmente para produzir conteúdo legítimo para empresas, restaurantes, clientes e campanhas publicitárias.

Se a preocupação é proteger a identidade das pessoas, ótimo. Mas é preciso encontrar um equilíbrio entre segurança e usabilidade.

Uma ferramenta de IA precisa proteger as pessoas sem transformar qualquer pessoa real em um bloqueio automático.

Eu gostaria muito de continuar utilizando o CapCut e suas ferramentas de IA, mas, do jeito que está, a experiência passa a ser extremamente frustrante para quem trabalha profissionalmente com produção de conteúdo.

Espero que a equipe reveja essas limitações e encontre uma forma de permitir usos legítimos e autorizados, sem comprometer as políticas de privacidade e segurança.

Obrigado pela atenção.
1500855883.title: IA

Estou extremamente frustrado com o CapCut. Uso a plataforma para trabalhar na geração de vídeos por IA vive apresentando erro.

Em uma das tentativas, inclusive, coloquei créditos justamente para conseguir gerar o vídeo. A geração falhou, o vídeo não foi criado e, mesmo assim, os créditos foram consumidos. Ou seja: paguei pelo serviço, não recebi o que solicitei e ainda perdi os créditos.

Espero que o CapCut resolva esse problema, devolva os créditos consumidos indevidamente e melhore urgentemente a estabilidade da ferramenta.

948660805.content:
Ein Paradebeispiel für die Erfolgsaussichten einer „digitalen Souveränität – Made in Germany“

Wir schreiben das Jahr 2026. Sechs Generationen Apple Silicon haben inzwischen das Licht der Welt erblickt, und der M6 verrichtet längst sein Werk in den Maschinen unserer Tage. Die Intel-Ära ist Geschichte; Apple Silicon längst vom kühnen Versprechen zur alltäglichen Wirklichkeit geworden.

Doch fernab dieses rastlosen Zuges der Zeit scheint man bei Governikus eine beschaulichere Vorstellung von technischem Fortschritt zu pflegen. Dort reist die AusweisApp noch immer auf den alten Gleisen der Intel-Ära und lässt sich von Rosetta über die Zeiten tragen – jener ehrwürdigen Brücke, die dereinst für einen kurzen Übergang errichtet ward und auf der man sich nun offenbar häuslich eingerichtet hat.

Derweil verkündet der deutsche Staat mit gewichtigen Worten die „digitale Souveränität“. Man spricht von Unabhängigkeit, technologischer Selbstbestimmung und einer modernen digitalen Verwaltung.

Welch erhabene Worte.

Allein, auf dem Mac genügt ein Blick auf die AusweisApp, und der Glanz der Zukunft bekommt einen eigentümlich nostalgischen Schimmer.

So schreiben wir das Jahr 2026: Der M6 ist angekommen. Die digitale Souveränität wird verkündet. Und während die Welt längst das andere Ufer erreicht hat, verweilt Governikus mit der AusweisApp noch immer auf der Brücke namens Rosetta.

Und während man dort noch auf alten Brücken wandelt, wurde andernorts die Berliner Verwaltung Opfer eines folgenschweren Cyberangriffs samt Datendiebstahl und Erpressung.

Wen wundert’s.

Doch sorgen wir uns nicht: Über allem weht schließlich das große Banner der „digitalen Souveränität“. Nur mit der digitalen Wirklichkeit scheint es bisweilen noch nicht recht Schritt halten zu können.

— Ein IT-Spezialist mit Schwerpunkt IT-Sicherheit

1113153706.content:
The Teams app really lacks support for older iOS devices compared with what Skype offered.

For people who simply want to make audio and video calls, Skype was straightforward and accessible, including on older devices. Since Skype was retired and users were moved towards Teams, I haven’t really used Teams at all because of the lack of support for older devices. Instead, I’ve ended up using Signal for video and audio calls.

I think Microsoft could attract many more users by introducing a lightweight “Teams Lite” app designed specifically for audio and video calling. It could include basic calling, contacts, messaging and notifications, without all the additional Teams features that many casual users simply don’t need.

A simple, lightweight version with wider support for older iOS devices would make Teams a much more practical replacement for Skype.

クロードの使い方は人それぞれだと思うが、個人的にこのアプリを使うなら調べ物くらいにした方がいい。創作で使うのはおすすめしない。創作のサポート、たとえば独自設定との齟齬がないかの確認もかなり怪しい。また実際に執筆させる場合には、ユーザーの設定は一貫して適用されないのでかなりストレスになる。なので、使うなら短編で、あまり設定を盛り込まない方が精神衛生上で安心できる。反面、AIの持つテンプレート文章の切り貼りになるのでつまらない。そこを割り切って使えるならそれでいいと思う。クロードは「辻褄合わせ」「ツギハギ」が得意。1箇所の修正でも、前後の流れが変わるかもしれないけど、1箇所しか直さないからチェックは欠かせない。
設定ファイルを読み込ませても、「読み込んだだけ」で内容に反映されないことが多い。プロンプトは丁寧に詳細に書いておいた方がいい。ただ、そこまでできる人なら一から自分で執筆する方がストレスフリーで効率的です。

545519333.content:
Amazon Prime Video used to be a great streaming service, around 2018/19, that’s gone steadily downhill in the years since. The worst of it though typically was confined to the ui. But now they make even the basic video playback painful to use. You cannot watch anything without that awful button appearing at just the worst moment telling you to skip the tv intro for no good reason. It’s obnoxious and totally takes me out of the mood. It’s like a turn off for tv. I don’t know who invented such a pointless “feature” —there’s no reason you couldn’t just skip forward 10s a few times if you really wanted to skip so badly—but nobody ever would want to use such a preposterous feature in the first place.

The theme tune and intro is an iconic thing. You look forward to it. You get a release of emotion. Often cliffhangers from the teaser will build up to it, and that tune kicking in is the release.  You can’t remove such an integral part! And asking me to just endure the obnoxious, ugly button is not a reasonable solution, to pretend like it’s not there. It’s a giant wart on the screen whose very existence hurts the experience even if you never click it, because it suggests that skipping is something you might ever want to do, and that suggestion is offensive. It’s insulting to the quality of the program I’m watching, implying it’s not that important to be taken seriously.

I seriously hope Amazon developers take note of this problem and at the very least add in an option in settings to disable the button, if not remove it entirely in a future update. Autoplaying videos was similarly distasteful in the past when they were forced on us, but Amazon listened, and autoplay later became optional and able to be turned off. I hope the same happens for skip intro/recap buttons.

On a positive note, I actually really like the newest ui in this latest redesign. As I said earlier, it had gone in a wrong direction before, but now it’s getting better. It harkens back to the iOS 6 and earlier days, when graphics had depth, gradients, 3D effects, shadows, etc. and looked very polished and professional. Just too bad that stuff doesn’t matter much when the actual video playback has issues.
545519333.title: “Skip Intro” Buttons Ruin the Experience

6741796873.content: TikTok developers urgently need to optimize memory usage for mobile game streaming on iOS. Currently, streaming high-performance games causes the broadcast to instantly crash with a "Stream URL Error" whenever you open the in-app chat drawer during gameplay. This occurs because iOS caps screen recording extensions (ReplayKit) at a strict 50MB RAM limit, and rendering the live chat overlay forces the app over this ceiling, causing iOS to terminate the broadcast extension. The exact same account and settings work flawlessly on Android devices without any crashes. Please release an update for iOS that optimizes ReplayKit memory allocation and reduces overlay memory consumption so creators can manage chat without losing their stream!

6760173601.content:
Here’s a much more detailed version that focuses on the core problem: you asked it to do work, and instead of helping complete the work, it repeatedly refused.

★☆☆☆☆ Extremely disappointing — I downloaded this to get work done, and it repeatedly refused to do the work I asked for.

I downloaded Muse specifically because it was presented as an AI capable of helping with serious document work. My experience was the complete opposite.

I gave it clear instructions, explained what I needed, provided context, and tried multiple times to work within what it said it could do. Instead of actually helping me complete the task, I kept getting refusals, limitations, and explanations about why it would not proceed.

That is what made the experience so frustrating. I wasn’t looking for an AI to lecture me about what it wouldn’t do. I needed a tool that could understand the assignment, identify what parts it could legitimately help with, and then actually help me move the work forward.

Even when I adjusted my request and tried different approaches, it felt like I kept hitting the same wall. Rather than finding a useful path forward, Muse seemed more interested in explaining its boundaries than accomplishing the work.

For something marketed as a productivity tool, that defeats the entire purpose. If I have to spend more time negotiating with the AI than I would spend doing the work myself, then the AI isn’t increasing my productivity — it’s becoming another obstacle.

What made it worse was that some basic work could be completed, which initially made the product seem promising. But once I needed more substantial assistance, the usefulness dropped dramatically. The experience went from “this might actually save me time” to repeatedly arguing with software about whether it would help me.

I use AI because I expect it to help me organize complicated ideas, work through problems, create professional material, and find practical ways to accomplish a task. I understand that every AI has boundaries, but there is a major difference between having reasonable limits and making the user feel like the answer to everything meaningful is simply “I can’t help with that.”

That’s ultimately why I’m giving Muse one star. It refused to work on the work I actually needed it for. The problem wasn’t one isolated refusal; it was the overall experience of repeatedly trying to get meaningful work accomplished and repeatedly being stopped.

I expected a capable productivity assistant. What I experienced felt unnecessarily restrictive, frustrating, and inefficient.

There are too many AI tools available now for me to spend this much time fighting with one just to get basic productivity out of it. I deleted the app and won’t be recommending it.

1/5. A productivity tool shouldn’t create more work than it saves.
